questions.question: When backing with a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: You should not back up in a straight line.
You should not correct drift until you are far off course.
Pull forward often to reposition the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward often to reposition the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When backing, pull forward to reposition your vehicle as needed. Turn the steering wheel right away if the trailer drifts.

questions.question: Which of these is a sign of aggressive driving?

options.text: Slow down and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving. Plan ahead for delays, keep a safe distance from other cars, and do not make hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Question how well other people drive.

questions.explanation: Plan ahead with realistic travel times to avoid frustration and aggressive driving. Drive at a safe speed, keep a safe distance from other cars, do not make gestures at other drivers, and keep both hands on the wheel.

questions.question: What should you do if the brakes cannot build hydraulic pressure?

options.text: Hold the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.explanation: If your brakes will not build pressure, shift to a lower gear, pump the brakes, and use the emergency brake.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They are illegal in most states.
They help drivers see a wider area.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help drivers see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are curved and let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Non-front tires on a commercial vehicle must have a tread depth of at least ____.
questions.explanation: Front tires need 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. Other tires need 2/32 of an inch of tread depth.

questions.question: While driving, you should be aware of:

options.text: Only what is in front of your vehicle.
What is happening on all sides of your vehicle.
Only what is in front and to the sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: What is happening on all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always know what is happening around your entire vehicle. Look ahead and check your mirrors regularly on both sides.

questions.question: When you apply the brakes, your vehicle should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side while braking, it may be a brake problem.

questions.question: Wheel bearings and seals should be:
questions.explanation: Check that wheel bearings and seals are not leaking during an inspection.

questions.question: Are wheels with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if a professional did the repair.
Yes, if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Do not use wheels or rims that have been welded. Replace them before driving.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth required for rear tires?
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. Rear tires need at least 2/32 of an inch of tread depth. All tires on a vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will activate
The service air line will activate

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If air pressure is lost in this line, the emergency trailer brakes will activate automatically.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road
Tires are not made for wet weather
Water has not yet absorbed dirt and grease

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, water mixes with oil and grease on the road surface. This creates a slick film before the water washes the oil and grease away.

questions.question: Drivers talking to passengers should be considered:
questions.explanation: Talking to passengers takes a driver's attention away from driving. Use extra caution when driving near distracted drivers.

questions.question: If you realize you may be running late, you should:

options.text: Accept it and drive at a safe speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Accept it and drive at a safe speed
questions.explanation: To prevent aggressive driving, manage your stress. If you will be late, take a deep breath and accept the situation. Drive safely instead of speeding.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, a vehicle should:
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when you start from a complete stop. This prevents hitting anything behind you.

questions.question: People working on a disabled vehicle:

options.text: May not be paying attention to traffic
Do not have to follow traffic laws

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be paying attention to traffic
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people who are working on a disabled vehicle. They are focused on the repair and may not notice nearby traffic.

questions.question: Which factor should NOT affect how much liquid to load into a tank?

options.text: How much the liquid will expand while being transported

questions.explanation: Consider how much the liquid will expand, its weight, legal weight limits, and temperature when loading a tank. Driver speed does not affect how much liquid is safe to load.

questions.question: When stopping, apply the brake pedal by:
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. Gradual braking helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Hazardous materials should be loaded:
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Some materials cannot be loaded in spaces with heaters due to fire and explosion risks.
